newsitem.title: USA: Fed's Phillips sees resumption of consumer buying.
newsitem.headline: Fed's Phillips sees resumption of consumer buying.

text.p: Federal Reserve Board Governor Susan Phillips Friday said there is strong reason to believe that consumers will resume spending, leading to a good holiday season for retailers.

In an interview with Reuters, Phillips said that the overall economy looked good and that it appeared for now it would remain on a moderate but sustainable growth path, contingent upon a resumption of consumer spending.
"I think there are some pretty good reasons for a resumption of consumer spending," she said, citing upbeat consumer attitudes brought in part by a strong job market.
"The bottom line is people are working," she said, adding that "there are anecdotal reports from around the country of labor shortages in some sectors and some regions."
But she said that housing, which has weakened of late, was an unknown, although the decline of long-term interest rates held out the hope that this sector could strengthen.

"We've had a flattening out or decline in housing markets but on the other hand with the decline of long-term interest rates it is certainly feasible we could see some support for housing," she explained.
She estimated that the economy in the current quarter could grow by in a range of 2 to 2-1/2 percent or perhaps better.
"We don't have a lot of hard numbers in (for the fourth quarter) but I guess I would think in terms of a range of 2 to 2-1/2, maybe higher, but that is the range I've been focusing on," she said.
For next year, she said it was possible that the economy could grow faster than the Fed central tendency forecast last July showing a range of 1-3/4 to 2-1/4 percent in real Gross Domestic Product.
"It could be, I certainly think it is feasible , but I don't have a point estimate," she said.
Turning to inflation, she made clear that the core rate with energy and food costs subtracted had behaved well in recent times although food and energy costs alone had been more troublesome.
But she said that food costs should moderate in the period ahead as the impact of a better than expected harvest begins to take affect.
"We had a better crop situation this year so we're hopeful some of these price pressures will dissipate," she said.

On the other hand, energy costs may be being affected to some extent by greater global demand due, in part, to increased use in the emerging economies and this could help keep pressure on prices, she agreed.
"Some of these newly industrialized countries are going to continue to press on demand," she said, adding "I certaintly see energy as a significant risk in respect to inflation."

Asked about a key proposal under consideration by the Fed to expand the amount of activity that so-called section 20 subsidiaries of bank holding companies can undertake in the securities arena, Phillips said she was hopeful the board would consider it next month.
The proposal would allow these subsidiaries to derive 25 percent of total revenues from those activities, up from the current 10 percent.
